newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- APRIL 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- APRIL 14.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
IMERISIA

--A new bill soon to be submitted to Parliament will introduce new guidelines for mergers and buyouts of credit institutions and banks in an effort to adjust existing legislation to new conditions and streamline procedures.
--The new bill is geared to facilitate three major mergers in the domestic banking system - the mergers of Eurobank and Interbank, National Mortgage and Housing and of Commercial with Ionian.

--The national economy ministry is preparing three changes to the development law which will make improve the effectiveness of this year's 170-billion-drachma subsidy programme. The most important change involves banks being entrusted with the evaluation and selection procedure.
--CPI-indexed bonds will be issued at the beginning of May while demand for fixed rate bonds remains strong and steady.
KATHIMERINI (Sunday)

--The continued deceleration of interest rates is creating conditions for the real improvement of price levels on the ASE, attracting new capital to the money market. As part of efforts to protect this new capital, the government is pursuing its new 10-point plan to ensure transparency and ward off trading games.

--Unemployment in Greece - concentrated primarily in urban centres - can only be dealt with with bold steps that facilitate investment and boost competition. However, the government appears unprepared to take these steps.

--The latest reports are that tax revenues for the state have all but bottomed out, with certain government officials talking about the need for urgent new measures over summer to ensure budget targets are met. The rate of increase for revenues in March, according to reports, was zero, which brings the figure for the first three months to approximately 7.0 percent, compared to a forecast 14.6 percent. In real terms, this means a discrepancy for the state of some 120 billion drachmas so far.

--Greek telecoms organisation OTE is considering allowing current share holders the option of another six new shares for each 80 held and putting a ceiling on the sale of shares, in its imminent second offer.
TO VIMA

--The 800 billion drachmas owed by state organisations and ailing enterprises and the cost of servicing the debt are making a significant dent in the state budget and were the focus of concerns at last Thursday's meeting of the governmenbt's economic team. The black hole affecting the state of the public debt is epxected to increase next year.

--New legislation will establish a watchdog organisation staffed by judicial officials and experts to investigate procurements competitions in the public sector. The Greek state is paying about 500 billion drachmas per year in uncontrolled state procurements contracts, Deputy Development Minister Mihalis Chrysohoidis says, totalling 1,500 billion drachmaas, or 15 percent of GDP.

--The government's plans to denationalise the Athens Stock Exchange are going ahead with the evaluation report on the ASE recently pricing the insitution and its subsidiaries at 100 billion drachmas. The ASE's first year as a societe anonyme last year brought it profits of more than 2.4 billion drachmas.
--The National Bank of Greece is preparing to introduce its shares to the London market at the same time as it goes ahead with its share capital increase in the autumn.
ISOTIMIA

--The solution to falling returns from rate cuts in deposit accounts and state titles can be found in the investment mix of mutual funds, bonds and international gilt-edged bonds, bringing interest returns of between 15-25 percent.

--The bourse's general price index has stabilised at levels above 1,400 points, bolstering hopes of a further rise in prices in the near future. ING Baring on Friday outlined the prospects for the ASE in London.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
